puzzles.summary: Red timed ! run: five pink crates along the path after the switch.
puzzles.solution: Stop at the red ! (GR), hit it, sprint the path breaking all five before they fade.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Breaking the crates before the ! on the run, or detouring.

puzzles.summary: Three-high stack: pale crate on TNT on crate.
puzzles.solution: Knock out the bottom crate; the TNT drops lit; step away; the blast takes the top crate.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Spinning the TNT at chest height or standing beside it.

puzzles.summary: TNT under a strong crate at the bonus door, among shielded enemies.
puzzles.solution: Jump and whirlwind into the strong crate from above; leave the TNT for last and light it from range.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Whirlwinding into the stack at ground level sets the TNT off in contact.
puzzles.loss: A life (and the checkpoint is far back).

puzzles.summary: Bonus loop: framed TNT, pillar row with a ! under a strong crate, Nitro/fruit pairs, far-end Nitro switch, return sweep, final column.
puzzles.solution: Out: blow the framed TNT early, bounce to the pillar TNT, hit the ! under the strong crate, jump the pairs, press the Nitro switch. Back: sweep to the entrance (newly solid crates). Out again: the column on the pillar's far side, then the exit saucer.
puzzles.wrongOrder: Heading for the exit after the Nitro switch (the return sweep holds 7 + 3 crates); letting the outline frame close on the first TNT.
puzzles.loss: Up to 10 bonus crates for skipping the return; the framed TNT if sealed.

puzzles.solution: Light the TNT and retreat; the blast takes the Nitro and the stack.
puzzles.loss: A life at the end of a no-checkpoint corridor.

observations: Two powers reshape the crate grammar. The Ika-Ika gravity mask, taken at crate ≈ 17, puts crates on a floor you can no longer stand on (S4-a). The Akano whirlwind, at C4, makes long corridors of stacks safe to clear at a run.

TNT is the counter-design to the whirlwind: every TNT in a whirlwind stretch sits under or beside crates (S5-a, S5-b, S6-b, S7-a, S8-d), so a spin through the stack is lethal and the player has to light TNT deliberately.

The 34-crate bonus (22 % of the level) is a loop: out to a far-end Nitro switch, back to the entrance for crates that only now exist, and out again for a column on the far side of a pillar. Ten of its crates are behind the player at the moment the room looks finished.

The bonus mixes two outline behaviours: outline crates that a ! turns into breakable crates (counted), and 'invisible blocks' that turn into iron after a delay. Iron can seal a TNT inside its frame, so the room's first lesson is to act before the frame closes.
The shifting-wall room has no breakable crates at all: iron crates are only footholds. A pure platforming beat between two dense stretches.
Laser architecture paces the early crates: 2-stacks stand in the safe pockets between blinking gates (S1-b), and ? crates sit between floor beams (S1-c), so crate rhythm equals hazard rhythm.

Density curve: 16 / 16 / 6 / 11 / 14 / bonus 34 / 18 / 8 / 29. The final 29 are a 'no tricky crates' victory lap with the reacquired whirlwind, ending on a Nitro-capped TNT stack that pays the last 4 in one chain.

Checkpoints at 16, 32, 38, 49 and ≈ 124: the front half is checkpointed every 6–16 crates, then 75 boxes (including the bonus) pass without one. That run is made survivable by the multi-hit tool rather than by checkpoints.
The hidden gem uses the new power immediately: flip gravity before the first laser of the second vent and fall into a ceiling pocket (LP2 1:03:31). No crates are tied to it.
